q: How does a private tour work?
a: You get your own air-conditioned car or van with an English-speaking driver-guide for the whole trip, with no other passengers. We agree the route with you before you arrive, meet you at the airport, and you can change plans day by day.

q: How much does a tour cost?
a: Tours are priced per person per day for the vehicle and driver-guide. For one to three people travelling by car it starts at $65 per person per day on tours of a week or longer; groups of four to twelve travel in a van. Children under 12 are free. Tell us your group size and dates and we will send you the price, including any seasonal offer.

q: What is included, and what isn't?
a: Included: your private vehicle and driver-guide, fuel and parking, airport pickup and drop-off, and passenger insurance cover up to LKR 500,000. Not included: hotels, meals, entrance tickets, safari jeeps and flights. We will tell you the current ticket prices when we plan your route.

q: Can you book hotels for us?
a: Yes. Tell us your budget (budget, standard or luxury) and we will suggest and book hotels along your route, priced separately so you can see exactly what you pay for. You can also book your own hotels and we will plan around them.
Yes. Depending on your travel dates you can save 10–20% on the daily rate (shoulder season and green season), plus an extra 10% for tours of 14 days or more. See the seasonal offers above.

q: Are your tours suitable for families with children?
a: Yes. We plan shorter driving days and child-friendly stops such as the Elephant Transit Home, beaches and easy walks. Children under 12 are not charged for the vehicle and guide.

q: Do you do airport transfers only?
a: Yes. Transfers from Bandaranaike International Airport (CMB) start at $25, with meet-and-greet at arrivals. Day trips with a driver start at $45 per day.

q: When is the best time to visit Sri Lanka?
a: December to April is the dry season for the west and south coasts, Colombo, Kandy and the hill country. May to September is best for the east coast (Trincomalee, Arugam Bay). The Cultural Triangle is dry for most of the year apart from October to December.

q: How far in advance should we book?
a: For December to March, two to three months ahead is best, as good hotels and reserved train seats sell out. Outside peak season we can often arrange a tour within a few days.

Most visitors need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travelling, and some nationalities can enter visa-free. Check the official site eta.gov.lk for your passport. We are happy to help if you have questions.
